selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.

plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether a periodic quarter-wave stack design, based on recalled thin-film optics principles, can achieve dual-band performance (high visible reflectance, high telecom transmission) using HfO2/SiO2 on fused silica. The route varies individual layer thicknesses around quarter-wave optical thickness at ~550 nm center wavelength while keeping the 24-layer periodic topology fixed. Prior knowledge suggests this should work, but exact indices, optimal pair count, and angle sensitivity are uncertain without literature lookup.

routes.title: Quarter-Wave Stack Thickness Optimization for Dual-Band Dichroic Filter
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 24-layer periodic HfO2/SiO2 stack with optical thicknesses tuned around quarter-wave at 550 nm will achieve high reflectance in 400-700 nm while maintaining high transmittance in 1530-1565 nm, with best_target_score increasing as thickness optimization converges toward the quarter-wave condition.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave optical thickness (n×d = λ0/4) at the center of the rejection band creates constructive interference for reflection at that band. The high index contrast between HfO2 (~2.0-2.1) and SiO2 (~1.45-1.5) provides sufficient reflectance per interface. The telecom band at ~3× the visible center wavelength falls outside the primary stopband, allowing transmission.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | sio2 substrate (24 layers total, 12 pairs, starting with HfO2 at Air interface)
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 24 layers (24 independent thickness variables in nm)
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 400-700 nm band
Minimize thickness variation from quarter-wave nominal values as secondary preference
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 24 (within 30-layer limit)
Individual layer thicknesses should remain manufacturable (typically >20 nm for stability)
HfO2 and SiO2 are both standard evaporatable/sputterable materials
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory: maximum reflectance occurs when each layer has optical thickness λ0/4 at the center wavelength of the stopband
Stopband width scales with index contrast: Δλ/λ0 ≈ (4/π)×arcsin((nH-nL)/(nH+nL))
Higher pair count increases peak reflectance asymptotically toward unity
Transmission bands occur at wavelengths outside the stopband, with secondary stopbands at odd harmonics
expected_advantages: Simple, well-understood design pattern from recalled thin-film practice
Periodic structure reduces optimization complexity compared to aperiodic designs
HfO2/SiO2 pair provides good index contrast for visible band rejection
24 layers provides margin within the 30-layer manufacturing constraint
known_risks: Refractive index values for hfo2 and sio2 at specific wavelengths are recalled approximations only - exact values from material_catalog datasets would confirm quarter-wave thickness calculations
Optimal center wavelength for the visible stopband is assumed to be 550 nm without verification against the 400-700 nm requirement
Normal incidence is assumed; angle sensitivity was not analyzed and could affect spaceborne performance
12 pairs (24 layers) was chosen from recalled practice but may not be optimal - fewer pairs might suffice or more might be needed
Secondary stopbands from the quarter-wave stack could appear near telecom band (3rd harmonic relationship) and require verification
What would settle these: look up exact n(λ) data from material_catalog, calculate quarter-wave thicknesses explicitly, verify stopband positions against both wavelength bands
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 24-layer periodic dielectric stack on SiO2 (Lemarchand) substrate with Air incident medium. Materials: alternate hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand), starting with hfo2 at the Air interface. Optimize all 24 individual layer thicknesses to maximize transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band and maximize reflectance in 400-700 nm band. Normal incidence assumed. Total layers fixed at 24. Materials must resolve to hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) from material_catalog.

Whether 12 pairs is optimal or if 10-14 pairs would perform better
Whether 550 nm is the optimal center wavelength for the visible stopband

Whether secondary stopbands near telecom wavelengths will interfere with transmission
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If this control route fails to achieve meaningful dual-band separation (best_target_score remains below 0.5 after exhaustion), the fundamental quarter-wave approach may be insufficient for this wavelength ratio, and a more complex aperiodic or multi-cavity design would be needed.

expected_observations: best_target_score should increase across optimization rounds as thicknesses converge toward quarter-wave condition for visible band
valid_candidates should remain high (near total candidates) since quarter-wave stacks are physically realizable
tightest_margin should not decrease significantly across rounds if the design is robust
thicknesses_nm should converge toward values consistent with quarter-wave optical thickness at ~550 nm center wavelength
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates drops below 50% of total candidates for two consecutive rounds, relax thickness bounds and continue
if tightest_margin falls below 0.1 for two consecutive rounds, reduce optimization step size and continue
